data_origin: Controlled graph-based mixture identifiability problem using ordinary ester/acid examples. No actual spectrum, reaction or instrument selectivity is claimed.
identity_policy: Deduplicate exact neutral graph identities while preserving stereochemistry, charge and all components; each molecular species has ONE mole fraction regardless of record multiplicity. Name each species by its lexically smallest source ID. Do not canonicalize tautomers, remove fragments or neutralize.
response_model: All components belong to the compatible neutral-mass panel and obey the absence-of-free-acid constraint. An unknown nonnegative mole-fraction vector sums to one. For each specified SMARTS, a pure-species response equals its complete ordinary graph match count with unique atom-tuple matches, use_chirality=true, tautomer_aware=false; every graph occurrence is equally calibrated. An observed response is its exact mole-fraction-weighted mean. These are ideal selective motif channels, NOT assignments of real NMR peaks. Retain ALL compatible compositions; do not choose a minimum-norm mixture as identified.
design_policy: For each candidate assay, append its pure-species match-count row to the present normalized response equations. It is identifying only if any two currently feasible compositions with the same new exact response must be identical. Select the least-cost identifying assay; ties use lexical ID. No future response is provided. Compute the sharp premeasurement interval for the selected assay over the entire present feasible set.
reporting: Return eligible_species_ids after identity/mass/free-acid qualification, deduplicated_source_groups (only groups of at least two equivalent source records), sharp_mole_fraction_intervals keyed by every eligible species ID, mixture_is_point_identified, selected_assay_id and selected_assay_response_interval. Use 1e-7 absolute plus 1e-7 relative tolerance; arrays of IDs/groups are unordered. Distinguish eligibility from a positive lower bound on abundance.

research_motivation.scope: Mixture quantification and signal overlap motivate the question; motif counts here are an explicitly controlled response model, not empirical peak selectivity.
